notes: Market fair is the books' price on both sides with the hold removed, averaged across the books quoting the most common line. When the books' yardage lines differ, each book's price is first moved to the middle line, so the count can include books that posted a nearby line.
A fair number needs two books pricing both sides of a prop (three books for anytime TD). Until then the prop shows its best price only.
Best is the best price any book we check posts at that line, as of when the lines were pulled. Prices move, so check the book before you bet.
Anytime TD is posted one way (yes only), so its market number is the average across books with their cut still in it. It runs higher than the true chance.
Game logs come from ESPN's box scores for this season and last, games against FCS schools included. A transfer's games from last season are with his old school.
Early in the season a window rests on a few games, so a hit rate or a defense's rank can swing on one game.

The defense numbers are what that defense allowed per game to the players it faced, over its own games against FBS offenses in the window you pick, ranked against every FBS defense. College box scores list no positions, so players are grouped by the role their stats show: a passer is a QB, then carries against catches split backs from receivers, and tight ends count as receivers, as on DraftKings. The colors read from the player's side: green when the defense is in the top third for giving up that stat, red in the bottom third, yellow in between. Interceptions and takeaways flip, since those are the defense's own plays. FCS defenses aren't ranked.
College stats count sacks as runs, so a quarterback's carries and rushing yards include his sacks.
Research, not picks: no edge, no lean, no bet recommended.

Our college projections are new. They split each team's expected volume, from the game's spread and total, by each player's recent share of it. Treat them as a first read. They cover DraftKings' main slate games only.
